hook: A still image captured by a U.S. military system showing a small unidentified object centered within a crosshair reticle, submitted by the FBI to AARO in 2025 after the original imagery was redacted and without any accompanying mission report.
why_it_matters: This case is notable because the military operator who captured the imagery was unable to positively identify the object, satisfying the baseline criterion for a genuine UAP report. The fact that the FBI redacted the original military imagery before forwarding it to AARO — the designated oversight body — raises questions about what information was withheld from the government's own disclosure process. The absence of a mission report further strips the image of the operational context that would be essential for any credible analysis.

key_findings.finding: The image was sourced from a U.S. military system and shows an unidentified object precisely centered within a targeting or tracking reticle, suggesting the system was actively tracking the object at the moment of capture.
The original military imagery was altered with redactions before being submitted to AARO, meaning the government's primary UAP oversight body received a degraded version of the source material.

No accompanying mission report was provided, removing the operational context — including platform type, altitude, speed, heading, and environmental conditions — that would be necessary to characterize the phenomenon.
The operator reported being unable to positively identify the UAP, establishing this as an unresolved case by the direct witness with access to the full operational picture.

The date displayed in the image is acknowledged to be incorrect due to the system's date/time not being set, introducing a metadata reliability issue that complicates temporal cross-referencing with other incidents.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This image was formally submitted by the FBI to AARO as part of the UAP reporting pipeline, making AARO the direct recipient and custodian of this case.
The image originates from an unspecified U.S. military system, which historically routes UAP-related sensor data through defense technical intelligence channels associated with Wright-Patterson.
